Multiple AEM instances. Separate folders. One desktop experience. Sambafied’s intended advantage is concurrent access to distinct AEM instances through separate work folders in one client. That complete simultaneous workflow is still under development. Named connection and mount primitives exist; they are not proof of end-to-end multi-instance readiness.

Adobe Experience Manager desktop app already supports native desktop work: opening and editing assets, revealing downloaded files or folders, and explicitly uploading local changes. See Adobe’s getting-started guide. Adobe also documents changing the connection to a different server. Its troubleshooting section explains that old cookies can interfere with authentication and prescribes logging out of the current session and clearing cookies before reconnecting in that situation. See Login issues when switching to a different server. That is evidence of a server-switching workflow. It does not establish that cookie clearing is always needed, or provide an explicit current-version statement that only one server/session can ever be connected. We do not turn the absence of documented concurrent mappings into proof that they are impossible.

Adobe’s v3 release notes describe automatic upload of new files under downloaded folders and collection synchronization. The comparison is about Explorer-first repository access and concurrent per-instance mappings, not a claim that Adobe has no sync or automatic upload behavior.

Question Adobe’s documented workflow Sambafied direction and boundary How do I reach assets? Native application open/edit and file/folder reveal actions. A native work folder as the starting point; bounded Windows/local AEM evidence exists. What happens across servers? Connection changes between servers are documented, with logout/cookie-clearing guidance for authentication interference. The reviewed sources do not document concurrent per-instance work-folder mappings. Multiple AEM instances available simultaneously in distinct folders, within one client. Complete concurrent operation still needs qualification. Does saving publish edits? Upload Changes explicitly sends local edits to AEM. Local save and remote publication are distinct. Bounded local adapters exist; production sync acceptance remains open.

For teams working across brands, environments, or repositories, evaluate whether assets from each instance can remain available side by side, whether their destinations are clear, and how independent authentication and publication behave. Sambafied’s multi-instance goal is to reduce connection switching as people move between repositories. It is a product direction, not a released feature or a promise of cross-instance migration. Sambafied is an independent project and is not affiliated with Adobe. No endorsement, feature parity, performance advantage, or certified compatibility is claimed. Check readiness and limits and multiple instances before evaluating.

Keep the local original, captured changes, and operation context until the outcome is known. A network error can mean a request failed before AEM changed—or that AEM changed but the response never arrived.

Observation Next step Another user changed the remote asset Recheck the remote version and review your local changes before publication. Upload returned an uncertain result Inspect the recorded operation and remote result before retrying. Sign-in expired Reauthenticate the intended connection; do not change the destination to get around the failure. A work folder is disconnected Inspect its exact root status and reconnect using its ownership information. A root is partially initialized or stopping Preserve it for explicit lifecycle recovery; do not create a fresh mount over it.

The bounded local publication path verifies a recoverable remote version before replacement. That helps recovery, but it does not establish atomic compare-and-swap protection against concurrent writers. Do not treat a check-out icon, a successful preflight hash, or a successful HTTP response as a universal conflict guarantee.

documents.t: Record the candidate build, connection, Author, account identity, work-folder path, action, and redacted error. Preserve the local file and pending generation. Avoid sharing credentials, session cookies, signed URLs, or sensitive asset contents in diagnostic notes. Do not rename, move, or delete retained agent state to clear a warning. A similarly named connection is not an equivalent destination.

Pausing the provider, closing a desktop window, quitting the agent, unregistering a root, and deleting files are separate operations. The inspected window lifecycle can leave the agent serving folders when the window closes. Use the folder lifecycle before unregistering and troubleshooting for connection and recall problems. Exact-build failure/recovery qualification remains distinct from source-level protections.
AEM as a Cloud Service and local AEM are both in Sambafied DAM Client’s product scope. Use a separate connection and work folder for each environment. The public product is coming soon.

Obtain the Author URL and account access for the intended Cloud Service environment. Do not substitute a delivery URL, a storage URL, or an unrelated Adobe service endpoint. For example, a Cloud Service Author URL looks like: https://author-p999999-e9999999.adobeaemcloud.com/ This is an example address. Replace p999999 and e9999999 with the project and environment identifiers in your actual Author URL, or copy the complete Author URL supplied by your AEM administrator. The inspected desktop connection design uses the Author’s own sign-in page. A Cloud Service Author can present Sign in with Adobe and continue through the organization’s identity flow. The desktop validates the resulting Author session before passing it to the agent. The provider hint in the connection UI is not itself proof that an operation is supported.

Record the exact candidate build and Cloud Service Author environment. Confirm the account can access the required DAM subtree. Complete the Author’s sign-in flow in the desktop window. Check the displayed principal and Author. Use a distinct, new empty local work folder and evaluate the explicitly enabled operations. If the candidate requires additional non-secret client configuration, use its matching instructions. Do not borrow another application’s client identity or treat a guessed OAuth registration as a supported integration. Illustrative sample. Review the Cloud Author address and deployment type.

A successful sign-in does not prove search, original download, upload, or processing completion. Cloud Service binary ingestion and on-premises binary writes use distinct adapters and eligibility checks. The source review retains open live Cloud Service and production-operation acceptance gates. This site therefore does not promise all operations for every Cloud Service environment, or infer Cloud readiness from a local Author result. Use readiness and limits to interpret the evidence. Multiple instances explains the intended side-by-side folder experience.

documents.t: Sambafied DAM Client is being built for local AEM and AEM as a Cloud Service. This guide covers the local Author path. The public product is coming soon; these notes describe the inspected development flow.

Have the exact Author URL, an authorized account, a dedicated evaluation DAM subtree, and a new empty work-folder path. Confirm the candidate build’s package identity and Cloud Files preflight before creating a fresh native root. For a standard local AEM Author running on this PC, enter: http://localhost:4502/ Use your actual Author address if its host or port differs. localhost refers to the PC running Sambafied; it does not point to an Author on another computer. Use HTTPS for normal environments. The development flow permits HTTP only when explicitly configured for a loopback Author; that exception is not a production network configuration.

Enter the Author URL in the desktop connection surface. Select Sign in. The embedded view opens the Author’s own login page. Complete the authentication presented by that Author. Verify the displayed account and Author before choosing the work folder. Select a new empty folder on a qualified local volume. A connection label that already belongs to another Author must not be silently reused. Give separate instances distinct names and destinations. The inspected flow validates the Author session before handing it to the agent. Remembering the connection is an explicit option; it does not replace server-side session checks. Illustrative sample. Review the local Author address and sign-in choices.

Open the work folder and recall a known test original. Confirm the bytes and the root status. A signed-in account and a populated folder are separate observations: sign-in alone does not prove the folder is connected. Local sign-in, mount, recall, logout, and remembered restore have bounded development evidence. That evidence does not qualify every production on-premises version, SSO profile, proxy, or certificate setup. See getting started for evaluation preparation, the folder workflow for retention, and Cloud Service connections for the other deployment path.

Towards a proper desktop experience. Getting an asset out of a DAM should not have to interrupt the work you opened it for. Find it in the portal, download it, find the download, open your editor, save a revision, then return to upload it: each hand-off is another chance to lose track of the right file. Sambafied is being built around a more connected Windows workflow: an AEM work folder in File Explorer, with assets available to the applications you already use. The goal is less file shuffling, not less visibility into where your work is saved. This page describes the intended experience and what to check in the Windows development preview. Application compatibility, uploads and recovery need confirmation for your build and AEM environment. It is not a production-readiness promise.

Imagine updating a campaign PSD stored in AEM. Instead of creating another download to keep track of, start with the connection's managed work folder. Find the right original. Open the work folder in Windows File Explorer and check that it belongs to the intended AEM connection. A listed file may still be cloud-only; seeing its name does not mean its contents are already on this PC. Open it in your usual application. Use the build's supported Open or Edit action and wait for the original to download. The intended folder experience also lets you reach assets through an application's file dialog. Check this with a small test asset before depending on a particular Photoshop workflow. Make and save your change. Save the managed working copy in the editor. A successful local save protects that local revision; it does not prove that AEM has received it. Review and upload deliberately. Return to Edited locally, check the saved copy and use Upload Changes when ready. Follow any checkout requirements separately. Do not assume that saving in an editor automatically uploads or checks the asset in. Verify the server result. Inspect Transfers and Operations, then confirm the intended revision in AEM. Where processing is required, check that separately from the binary transfer. Only then treat the change as available from the server. For the detailed actions, see opening and editing, native work folders and transfer results.

documents.t: The same idea applies when placing an image in a layout or opening a file from an application's Open dialog. A connected folder should make the asset easier to reach without downloading the entire repository first. Whether an application embeds a copy, keeps a link or supports a drag gesture depends on that application and your build. Check which file it uses and whether the original is locally available. Placing an image in a document does not mean edits to that document update the source asset in AEM. Use the supported file picker or Open action if a gesture is unavailable. See creative application workflows before relying on a particular editing or placement path.
documents.s: Bring the asset into the work, not another download folder

documents.t: Keep these states separate when evaluating the workflow: Listed remotely: the asset is visible, but its original may still need downloading. Available locally: the original can be opened on this PC; offline availability still needs checking. Edited locally: a newer save exists on this PC and may not have been uploaded. Transferring: work is in progress, not yet a confirmed server update. Confirmed in AEM: the intended revision is present on the server; any required processing or publishing is a separate check. These are workflow distinctions, not a promise of identical badges in every build. If a transfer fails or its result is unknown, preserve the local file and inspect the details before retrying. A cancelled request may already have completed on the server. A newer local save can also remain unuploaded after an earlier revision finishes transferring. See conflicts and recovery when the local and server copies no longer agree.
documents.s: Know which state your work is in

documents.t: Sometimes a separate copy is exactly what you want: a new campaign variation, an export for delivery or an independent local experiment. Use Save As or export deliberately, choose its destination and keep a clear name. An exported copy outside the managed work folder is independent of the connected asset. Editing it does not update the original in AEM. If you want it in the DAM, use the supported upload workflow and review the target folder, filename and collision choice. Do not use private cache folders as an import shortcut. The distinction matters: editing a connected working copy and creating a new asset are different tasks. See uploading files and folders.

The aim is not to replace every AEM screen. Use AEM's browser interface for the metadata, approvals, permissions, publishing and other governance tasks your organisation manages there. Use the desktop workflow for reaching originals and working in native applications, then verify the resulting asset in AEM. Browser actions explains how to keep the connection and asset destination clear when switching between them.

documents.s: Migrate from Adobe AEM desktop app

documents.t: Complete these steps before installing Sambafied: Back up local work. Export or save copies of any locally edited files that have not been uploaded to AEM. Check the Adobe app's Pending Changes or Modified files view. Note your connections. Record the AEM Author URLs, usernames, and DAM paths you currently use. You will need these to set up Sambafied. Document linked assets. If you have InDesign, Illustrator or Photoshop documents that link to AEM assets, note the current file paths. After migration, you may need to relink these. Clear the Adobe cache (optional). If disk space is a concern, use Adobe's built-in cache cleanup before uninstalling. Do not manually delete files. Uninstall Adobe (optional). You can run both applications side by side during evaluation. Uninstall Adobe only after you have verified Sambafied works for your needs.
See getting started for build instructions. Sambafied is currently a development preview built from source; a production installer is not yet available.
Launch Sambafied. Add a new connection using your AEM Author URL. Sign in when prompted. Choose a work folder location on a local NTFS drive in Windows. See Connections for detailed instructions.
documents.s: Step 2: Set up your first connection

documents.t: Browse to a folder you know exists in AEM. Open a test file to verify download works. Make a small edit and upload to verify write access.

If you have InDesign, Illustrator or Photoshop files that referenced assets through Adobe's desktop app: Open the creative document. The application will report missing links (the old paths no longer exist). Use the application's relink feature to point to the new Sambafied work folder location. Save the document. Important: Adobe's desktop app used paths like \\Server\ShareName\... on Windows. Sambafied uses a different path structure based on the Windows work folder you chose.
Repeat steps 2-4 for each AEM instance you previously connected to. Illustrative sample. Verify the named connection and work folder after migrating.

Adobe automatically creates a folder at a fixed location. Sambafied lets you choose where to store local copies. This gives you more control but requires you to remember where you put things.

Adobe requires separate app instances or profile switching. Sambafied supports named connections, each with its own work folder, making it easier to work with multiple AEM environments simultaneously.

Adobe uses Windows network share paths (\\AdobeServer\...). Sambafied uses Windows work folders such as C:\users\sambafieduser\Sambafied\PROD. Creative documents that linked assets through the old paths will need relinking.
Adobe has built-in offline caching. Sambafied's offline support is still under development. Check readiness and limits for current status.
Adobe uses its own credential management. Sambafied uses Windows Credential Manager after browser-based sign-in.
This is expected. Use your creative application's relink feature to update paths.
Check the Adobe cache folder location and back up any needed files before uninstalling.
Both applications work with AEM Assets, but supported file types depend on your AEM configuration, not the desktop app.
Performance depends on many factors: AEM server, network, file sizes and local disk speed. Evaluate with your typical workload.
You can run Adobe AEM desktop app and Sambafied side by side during evaluation. Use different work folder locations to avoid conflicts. Do not connect both to the same AEM folder simultaneously.

Downloads and release notes: updates.sambafied.me. Public channel releases are not available yet. If you received a tester ZIP, follow tester installation; those packages are updated manually.

When a signed release is available, open Sambafied downloads and choose its installation link. Open the downloaded .appinstaller file with Microsoft App Installer. Installing through this file registers the channel used for future updates. Beta contains preview releases for testing. Stable is intended for everyday use once available. Changing channels is an explicit installation from the downloads page; a lower version cannot replace a higher installed version.

For channel installations, Windows App Installer manages downloads, signature verification and installation. The Sambafied channel settings request update checks when the app launches and in the background. Your organisation's Windows policies can affect this behaviour. Updates can wait while Sambafied or its background Agent is running. Save work, let transfers finish and quit Sambafied from the tray when you are ready to update. Keep local assets, saved connections and recovery data in place.

In builds with About → Check for updates, use that action to open Windows App Installer for your installed channel. A development build or a package installed without a channel may open the downloads page instead. If an update fails, keep your existing installation and local data. Note the installed version and Windows error, then contact the person who supplied the build. Do not uninstall or delete caches as an update shortcut. Illustrative sample. Open About to check the installed app version and available controls.

Search options vary by server. Exact metadata fields and wildcard examples are still being prepared. Open search in My assets and enter a name, title or supported metadata query. Check whether the search covers the repository or only the current screen. Choose an available sort field and direction. Clear the query to return to browsing. Read the result count and any loading limit before treating the list as complete. If search fails, keep the query and retry. A local screen filter does not search the whole repository. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Check which rows are loaded and which actions are available. Select the assets using their selection controls. Check the selected count and the available common actions. Use Select All for the loaded rows. If an action offers all search results, inspect its separate review and complete count. Confirm the reviewed selection or cancel. A mixed selection may offer fewer actions than a single asset. Clear the selection to start again. If an action is unavailable, inspect individual status or select fewer items. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

documents.t: Select a readable asset. Open its details or preview. Inspect the title, file type, size and available metadata. Download the original when you need the full file. A thumbnail does not mean the original has downloaded. Preview and playback formats depend on the build. If a preview is missing, inspect metadata and retry. Read any original-download error separately. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Guide home · Find a task Collections group existing DAM assets. They do not create separate editing histories or independent copies. Browsing collections does not imply permission to change their membership. Collections are planned and are not available in the current connected client. Use My assets for current browsing. The following steps describe the intended flow for a future build that provides Collections. Ask your administrator about required server support; do not install additional server components yourself.

These steps are conditional on a future build providing Collections. Live AEM collection behavior has not yet been verified. Open Collections and refresh the list. Open a collection and check whether all members loaded. Browse members and review any download, including subfolders and related files. Inspect individual missing or denied items in Transfers. A collection groups existing assets. An incomplete member list does not mean it is empty. Cancel remaining downloads without deleting completed files. Ask your administrator about collection availability; do not install server components yourself. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

The same asset can appear in several collections and My assets. Shared editing behavior is still being checked. Open asset details and check its server location. Inspect local status before editing or downloading another copy. When accessing it through another collection, check that the same local work and checkout state appear. Collection membership does not create a separate asset or editing history. Removing membership differs from deleting the asset. If views disagree, refresh and preserve existing local edits. Do not create another working copy to hide the inconsistency. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Guide home · Find a task Preserve local edits before resolving conflicts. Compare the local and server copies; timestamps and checkout badges alone do not establish which version should replace the other. Keep recovery files and original connection details after a fault. Recovery should use the account and folder that own the work. Ask support before moving retained state, resetting credentials or discarding files to remove an error.

Be online and close applications writing the file. A current server original and protected recovery copy are required. Select the local edit and choose Discard Changes. Check the asset and the server copy that will replace it. Review the recovery copy and confirmation. Confirm only if this is the saved copy you intend to replace. Discard replaces the reviewed local edit. It does not delete the server asset, upload or check in. Cancel to keep edits. If recovery cannot be secured or the server state is unknown, stop and contact support. Illustrative sample. The discard confirmation identifies the original and the retained recovery copy.

Keep the local file and server information for comparison. Open conflict details. Compare revisions, sizes and timestamps. Use Reveal local or Open in Web if available. Keep an independent copy if unsure. To use the server copy, review local replacement and recovery before confirming. Use Refresh separately for a clean local copy. A lock icon or timestamp alone does not establish which copy should replace the other. Cancel to preserve local work. Resolve an unknown upload result before attempting another overwrite. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

documents.t: Guide home · Find a task Use Connections to check the server and account before acting. Give each connection a recognizable name. Ask your administrator for the correct Author address and DAM root; do not publish private environment addresses in screenshots or support reports. Sign-in methods depend on the server and build. Remembering the server address differs from remembering sign-in. If a session expires, sign in explicitly for that connection and check the account before resuming pending work.

Have the Author server address, deployment type and DAM root supplied by your administrator. Open Connections and choose the add connection action. Enter a distinct name, deployment type, Author address and DAM root. Connect, then check the displayed account and server. Edit the Explorer display name if needed. Before removing a connection, inspect its pending work. Each connection keeps its own account and work folder. Renaming a display label does not move files. See the PROD, STAGE and DEV folder examples when planning separate environments. Cancel setup to leave it unfinished. Keep local edits and recovery files if removal reports pending work. Illustrative sample. Connections lists named setups and sign-in status. Illustrative sample. The Connections filter includes active, signed-in and retained setups.

The supported sign-in method depends on the server and build. Select the connection and review its sign-in method. Before starting sign-in, choose Remember sign-in if offered and if you want this connection to retain its sign-in securely on this PC. This option is unavailable for the Native sign-in profile. Choose Sign in and complete the page or browser prompt presented by the app. Check the account name after connecting. Remembering the server address and remembering sign-in are separate choices. Cancel while sign-in is pending to abandon the attempt. If access is denied or the browser cannot return to the app, retry from that connection or ask your administrator. Never share sign-in tokens. Illustrative sample. The local Author form offers password sign-in and Remember sign-in on this PC. Illustrative sample. The Cloud AEM connection uses the SaaS deployment setting.

documents.t: Check which account owns local edits and pending transfers. Open Sign in again when the connection asks you to reconnect. Confirm the original account before resuming pending work. To sign out, choose Log out for that connection. To switch accounts, finish signing out, sign in again and check the new account before starting work. Local edits should survive session expiry and sign-out. Pending work belongs to the account that started it. If a different account appears, leave older pending work untouched and ask support for help. After restart, inspect Transfers before retrying an unknown result. Illustrative sample. A signed-out connection shows how to return to sign-in.

Guide home · Find a task Open uses an available original and its Windows application association. Linked creative documents also need related files, supported formats and stable paths. Exact application and version support is still being checked. Keep paths consistent across collaborators when documents depend on them. An exported copy is independent data outside the managed upload workflow. Changing an Explorer display name does not move the working files.

documents.t: Creative linking is still being checked for individual formats and application versions. Before opening or editing, inspect Include Related if available. Review dependencies and missing or ambiguous links. Use stable connected paths when placing assets in a creative document. Save locally, reopen to inspect links and upload reviewed changes separately. Downloading related files does not guarantee every creative application resolves its links. Preserve the document when links are missing. Use supported relink tools with care; do not edit binary links or guess replacement paths. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.
documents.s: Use related assets and linked documents

documents.t: Choose an ordinary local destination outside the managed work folder. Choose Export or Download a Copy. Review folder preservation or flattening, related files and naming conflicts. Confirm and inspect exported files and any partial-results list. Exported copies are independent. Editing them does not upload changes to the managed asset. Cancel remaining work where possible; completed copies may remain. Choose another name or destination instead of silently overwriting files. Illustrative sample. Download a copy shows the destination and files under review.

Guide home · Find a task Illustrative sample. The asset list distinguishes cloud-only and locally available files. Term Meaning Connection A named server, DAM root, account and work folder. Author server The AEM address supplied for managing assets. Original The full asset file, as distinct from a thumbnail. Work folder The managed Windows location for accessing originals. Cloud-only Visible in the folder, but its original still needs downloading. Available locally The original has downloaded to this PC. Pinned Requested to remain offline; check download progress for completion. Edited locally Saved changes on this PC that may still need uploading. Upload Changes Send a reviewed saved copy to the server. Processing Server work after transfer, which can finish later. Checkout A server reservation or ownership signal; enforcement varies. Check-in Release checkout where supported; separate from upload. Conflict Local and server changes need comparison before replacement. Unknown result The server outcome needs checking before retrying. Collection A group of existing assets, not separate copies. Alias Another view of the same asset, including through a collection. Display title A label, distinct from filename and folder location. Exported copy Independent local data outside the managed upload workflow. Recovery copy Data retained to protect local work during replacement or repair. Saved and effective settings The preference you saved and the value currently applied. Read moving from Adobe desktop app for practical differences.
Guide home · Find a task The intended Windows integration shows remote assets in a managed work folder and downloads originals when needed. A visible filename is not necessarily available offline.
documents.s: Native work folders and retained local data

documents.t: Keep the original folder, local edits and recovery data in place. If Recover existing work folders is offered, check the account, connection and folder before continuing. Cancel when they do not match. Supported customer recovery instructions remain in development; ask support before changing retained data. Explorer file changes do not necessarily mean a server rename or deletion succeeded. Check upload and operation status in the app. Changing a display label or saving a drive-letter preference does not move or map the folder. Illustrative sample. Import connections shows a retained work folder for review.

Use a Windows work folder configured by your build. Supported Windows versions and installation requirements are still being checked. Open the connection work folder in Explorer. Inspect cloud-only files and locally available originals. Open or download an original when needed. Use application connection controls to manage the work folder. A listing does not mean every original has downloaded. A display-name change does not move the folder. If a folder is unavailable or belongs to another setup, retain it and ask for recovery help. Do not unregister or move it manually. Illustrative sample. Choose your work folder shows the location Sambafied will use.

Use the original managed work folder. Recovery and editor compatibility are still being checked. Save in your desktop application. Return to Edited locally and inspect the saved copy. Before Upload Changes, review the copy selected for upload. After a crash or restart, inspect recovery messages and uncertain transfers before refreshing or uploading. A newer save can remain unuploaded after an earlier copy finishes uploading. Keep recovery files and edits when results are uncertain. Ask support to recover the original connection instead of deleting or moving its private data.

documents.t: The current client is for Windows only. For a supplied tester ZIP, follow tester installation. That page covers prerequisites, test certificate setup, installing the package and updating a tester build. Find downloads and release notes at updates.sambafied.me. Read automatic updates for the difference between a channel installation and a manually installed tester package. Sambafied AEM Desktop is a development preview; use the known issues supplied with your build.

Obtain the build from the responsible product contact. Check whether it is an offline demonstration or a connected client. The demonstration cannot sign in, upload assets or provide a real Windows work folder. For a connected build, ask your administrator for the Author address, DAM root, permitted sign-in method and disk requirements. Keep each connection's work folder distinct. Illustrative sample. Sambafied lists its Windows and work folder prerequisites.

Read Licensing to add your key, deactivate a device and locate the protected licence file. Full MSIX users must deactivate in the app before uninstalling; the license-aware Setup.exe does this automatically. Follow the instructions supplied with your build and preserve local work before removal.

Keep user work, recovery copies, cache and application configuration in place during updates. Changing a display name does not move a work folder. A supported migration procedure is still being prepared. Do not move existing application data into a proposed layout manually.

Use the tester installation steps for a tester ZIP, or the channel installation steps when signed releases are available. Obtain an evaluation build and instructions from the responsible product contact. Before updating, inspect pending uploads and back up local edits and recovery data. Follow only the update or rollback instructions supplied for that build. Before uninstalling, review data retention and keep user work by default. An evaluation build is not a supported customer release. Platform compatibility information will accompany a release. Stop if publisher, version or retention instructions are unclear. Do not delete caches or work folders as an upgrade recipe.
documents.s: Install, upgrade and uninstall without losing work

documents.t: Guide home · Installation Your Sambafied licence enables the desktop app on your device. Find your key in the License Portal guide or obtain it from Sambafied or your reseller. Activating Sambafied does not sign you into AEM. These instructions apply to builds with licensing enabled. Some evaluation builds report that licensing is not enabled. Sambafied remains a development preview; use the installation and known-issue notes supplied with your build.
documents.s: Add, manage and remove your licence

documents.t: Licence type Ownership and coverage Personal Licence Tied to one named person. It belongs to that individual and is for their use, rather than a shared licence for staff. Corporate Licence Belongs to the licensed company and covers all its staff. Staff covered by that corporate licence do not need individual personal licences. See pricing for personal pricing and corporate licence enquiries through a Sambafied partner. Licence ownership and device activation are different. Activation enables a PC for use under the licence; deactivating a PC does not change who owns the licence.

Connect to the internet before activating. Open Sambafied and choose About from the application menu. Select Manage licence. Paste your key into Licence key, then select Activate. Wait for the status to confirm activation. It also shows the offline licence expiry. Select Close when finished. If activation fails, check the key, your internet connection and the error message before retrying. If your device allowance is full, deactivate a device you no longer use or contact your licence provider. Keep your key private; do not include it in screenshots or support reports. Illustrative sample. The activation form has an empty Licence key field and an Activate button.

Open About > Manage licence to read the current status. Select Refresh licence online while connected to the internet to obtain an updated authorisation. An activated device can continue offline only until the expiry shown in the app. A licence may have a shorter term than the app's maximum offline period. Reconnect and refresh before it expires. An online refusal, expiry or invalid local licence may require activation or help from your licence provider. Illustrative sample. Manage licence shows activation status and the refresh action.

Deactivation releases this device's activation and removes its saved local licence. It does not cancel your licence agreement or delete DAM files, local edits, recovery copies or application settings. Finish or safely preserve pending work and connect to the internet. Open About > Manage licence. Select Deactivate this device. Select Confirm deactivation to confirm your choice. Wait for the message confirming that this device is deactivated. If deactivation fails, the local licence is retained so you can retry. Check connectivity and try again; contact your licence provider if it still fails. Closing the dialog before confirmation does not deactivate the device. For a personal licence, the named person remains the same when moving between PCs. To move to another PC, deactivate on the old PC first, then use the same key to activate on the new PC, subject to your licence's device allowance. If the old PC is unavailable, release its activation in the portal or ask your licence provider for help.
documents.s: Remove the licence from this device

documents.t: Preserve local edits and recovery data, follow the supported connection removal instructions, and quit Sambafied normally before uninstalling. If a managed work folder cannot be disconnected safely, stop and ask for help rather than deleting its files. Installation type Licence action Full MSIX package, including a tester MSIX Deactivate in the app before uninstalling. Windows package removal does not contact the licensing service to release the device. License-aware Setup.exe installer Uninstall automatically deactivates the device and removes its local licence before removing the app. An internet connection is required when an activation is saved. Older or other supplied build Follow its accompanying instructions; do not assume automatic deactivation is included. The license-aware Setup.exe stops uninstall if licence cleanup fails, a Sambafied process is still running, or a managed sync folder remains registered. Resolve the reported problem and retry. It preserves user files and settings. These installer behaviours are part of the current preview; complete installed testing is ongoing.

The app uses this location for the current Windows user: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sambafied\Licensing\[licence-scope]\licence.dpapi To inspect the folder, press Windows + R, enter %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sambafied\Licensing, and press Enter. The folder is created when a licence is saved. The long folder name under Licensing identifies the licensing configuration; it is not your licence key. For a typical profile, %LOCALAPPDATA% means C:\Users\YourName\AppData\Local. A full MSIX installation can use Windows-managed redirected app storage under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\[package-family-name]\LocalCache. If you cannot find the folder at the app's normal path, ask support to identify the location for your installed package. Windows describes this in its MSIX storage guidance. The licence.dpapi file holds the protected activation information, including the saved key and signed offline authorisation. Windows encrypts it for the current Windows user. It is separate from your DAM assets and settings; copying it is not a supported way to transfer a licence to another user or PC. Use the app to deactivate. Deleting the file or uninstalling an MSIX does not by itself release the remote device activation. Do not edit or delete the Licensing folder as a reset procedure. If the file is unreadable or corrupted, keep it in place and contact your licence provider for recovery instructions.
documents.s: Where is the licence stored on Windows?

Check the affected asset and destination before changing anything. A folder metadata schema defines available fields. Assigning a schema does not necessarily change descendants. documents.t: Have permission to change asset metadata. Choose Change Title. Inspect the current title and enter a new one. Review validation and save. Reopen details to check the result. Changing a title does not rename or move the file. Cancel to keep the title. If permissions or server changes prevent saving, keep the draft and refresh before trying again. Illustrative sample. Metadata editing depends on the server and available form. Choose Edit metadata. Inspect required, multiple-value and read-only fields. Make changes and review validation before saving. Reopen details to check saved values. Check the displayed result after submission. Preserve your draft if the asset changed or access was denied. Use Open in Web if desktop editing is unavailable and your administrator permits it. Illustrative sample. Have permission to create a folder in the selected parent. Choose Create DAM folder. Enter its name and title; inspect the final name and optional metadata schema. Review and confirm creation. Open folder properties to inspect location and metadata. Folder creation may succeed even if a later metadata step fails. If the name exists, parent is missing or access is denied, correct that issue first. Keep a successfully created folder and repair metadata separately. Illustrative sample. documents.t: A metadata schema defines folder fields. Have permission to change its assignment. Open the folder schema action, when available. Compare the current schema with the one you want to apply or remove. Review the affected folder and confirm. Reopen properties to inspect the result. Changing a schema does not necessarily change descendants. Cancel to retain the assignment. If assignment failed after folder creation, repair the existing folder rather than recreating it. documents.s: Apply or remove a folder schema

documents.t: Choose a supported destination on the same server connection. Choose Copy or Duplicate. Review destination and proposed name. Check which metadata, renditions, references and versions will be copied. Confirm and inspect the new asset. The original remains. The copy is a separate asset with its own editing and access state. Cancel to leave the source unchanged. If server copy is unavailable, export/import is a different procedure with different results. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Moving and filename renaming are planned; a supported customer procedure is not available yet. Keep the original asset and local edits in place. If your administrator offers an approved AEM web procedure, check pending edits, references and destination permission first. After an approved server change, refresh the desktop view and check linked documents. Changing a display title differs from renaming a filename. Do not rename cache entries as a substitute. Keep a safe copy and contact support if references are affected. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Remote deletion is planned; a supported customer procedure is not available yet. Review the asset or folder and preserve unuploaded work. Check descendants and references with your administrator. Use only an approved server deletion procedure, if available for your deployment. Server deletion affects other users. It differs from clearing a local download or removing collection membership. Cancel if scope or recovery is unclear. Do not delete work-folder files to attempt server deletion. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Guide home · Find a task Download originals and linked files while online before disconnecting. A thumbnail or filename does not guarantee offline access. State What it means Cloud-only Download the original while online. Available locally The original is on this PC; cleanup may reclaim eligible clean copies. Pinned or pending Retention was requested; check download completion. Edited locally Saved changes may still need uploading. Queued or uploading Inspect progress for the selected saved copy. Uploaded or processing Transfer and server processing may finish separately. Conflict Compare local and server versions before replacement. Unknown or detached Check the connection, account and result before acting.
If offered, automatic upload requires explicit opt-in for the connection. Check its policy and paused work before relying on it. Saving or pinning alone is not confirmation that a file uploaded.

Download the originals and linked files you need while online. Inspect local availability for each required asset. While offline, open only files whose originals are available on this PC. Save normally. Reconnect to the original connection and account before reviewing uploads. A visible cloud-only file is unavailable offline. Local edits remain separate from uploaded changes. If the account or server copy is uncertain, preserve local work and resolve the connection before refreshing or uploading. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

documents.t: Have enough disk space for the selected files and related assets. Select assets or a folder and choose Pin or Keep originals offline, when available. Review files, estimated space and related-file options. Wait for downloads and inspect partial or denied items. Unpin when you no longer need local retention. Pinning requests retention; only completed downloads are available offline. Unpinning does not delete the server asset or local edits. If space is insufficient, reduce the selection. Do not clear unuploaded edits to make room. Illustrative sample. Review which original to keep offline before confirming.

Guide home · Find a task Choose Open for viewing, Edit for making changes and Reveal to locate the file. Saving in a desktop application keeps work on this PC until you upload it. Checkout and check-in are separate server actions where supported. Related-file downloads and drag-and-drop vary by build and application. Use the available Open or Upload File action when a drag gesture is unsupported.
documents.s: Open, reveal, edit and check out

documents.t: Have a Windows application associated with the file type. Select the asset and choose Open. Use Open With to choose another application if offered. Wait for any original download before opening the file. Open uses the local original and does not automatically check the asset out. If no application opens, check the Windows file association and download status. Use Edit when you intend to change the asset. Illustrative sample. The selected asset menu shows Open and Open with.

Have edit permission and check whether your server supports checkout. Select the asset and choose Edit. Review any checkout message and download the original if needed. Make changes in your desktop application and save locally. Return to Edited locally, review the saved copy and choose Upload Changes when ready. Saving on this PC does not by itself upload changes. Check-in is separate where supported. If another person changed the server copy or owns checkout, preserve your local file and compare the versions before resolving the conflict. Illustrative sample. Select the edited file in Local edits to review what you saved.
documents.s: Edit, save locally and publish deliberately

documents.t: Select the asset or folder you want to locate. Choose Reveal or Show work folder. Check whether the destination is the work folder, selected asset, cache or an exported copy. Use the managed work-folder copy for editing and uploading changes. An exported copy is independent of the managed asset. If the destination is unavailable, inspect connection and download status. Do not move or delete cache files to repair it. Illustrative sample. Show work folder opens the folder for the active connection.

Drag-and-drop is still being checked across Windows and desktop applications. Use Open or Upload File when unavailable. For drag-out, download the original and select the asset. Drag to a supported destination and check whether it creates a copy or link. For drag-in, drop local files on the upload destination offered by the app. Review the target folder, filenames and collision choices before confirming. A drag gesture must not bypass the upload review. Cancel the review to stop an import. If a gesture fails, use the file picker rather than moving files into cache folders. Illustrative sample. Prepare native drag presents the selected file before dragging. Illustrative sample. The asset view indicates where files can be dropped.

Checkout and check-in depend on server support and permission. Inspect the asset checkout owner and status. Choose Check out to reserve it, if available. Upload saved changes separately when ready. Choose Check in and inspect the result. Treat checkout as advisory in this preview. A badge does not guarantee exclusive editing or replace conflict checking. If another person owns checkout or ownership changes, keep local work and ask your administrator. Upload does not necessarily check in. Illustrative sample. The checkout view shows ownership and local-state information.
documents.s: Check out or check in separately

documents.t: Guide home · Find a task Sambafied is intended to connect AEM Assets with a Windows work folder. You can find assets, open originals in local applications and review saved changes before uploading them.

Read installation and availability. Create a named connection with details from your administrator. Browse or search for a file you can read. Open the original, then use Edit and Upload Changes if you intend to change it. Inspect Transfers for the result. Illustrative sample. Home offers Browse files for the selected connection. Illustrative sample. My assets shows the files and folders in that connection.

A preview image is not a downloaded original. Saving in a desktop application does not automatically mean the server copy changed. Upload completion, server processing and check-in can happen separately. Keep local edits until you have checked the result.

An offline demonstration uses sample data. It does not connect to AEM, upload files or demonstrate Windows work-folder integration. Its simulated tray panel is part of the demonstration window. Ask the responsible product contact for demonstration launch instructions.
Guide home · Find a task

Sambafied AEM Desktop is in development. This manual does not announce a supported customer release. An approved public installer, signed release version, supported Windows/AEM combinations and public support destination are not available in this guide.

Obtain the build and instructions from the responsible product contact. Confirm whether it uses demonstration data or a live AEM connection. Check which features and server types that build supports. Preserve local edits before updating or uninstalling. Illustrative sample. Use About to identify the app when checking the notes for your build.

Exact customer installation, update and uninstall steps are pending. Filename move/rename and remote deletion have no supported customer procedure here. A full desktop version-history timeline is planned. Collection access, sign-in methods, browser integration, creative linking, Windows work folders, recovery and tray behavior still need build-specific validation.

Open relies on a Windows application associated with the file type and an available original. Preview, playback and linked creative-document support need separate format and application compatibility information. Adobe's compatibility list does not apply automatically to Sambafied. The task index lists intended workflows. Read each topic's availability notes before using it.

Guide home · Find a task Development preview. This Windows guide describes work in progress, not a supported customer release. Follow a procedure only when its controls are available in your build. Availability depends on the server and your permissions. Saved choices and their effects on Windows or background work are separate.

Open window at launch defaults to On. Activation, configuration or a prerequisite can still require the window to open. Start at login is a separate, optional request: an unchecked initial control does not establish that Windows startup is Off. Check the startup result shown by your build after changing it. Use the Window size controls to change dimensions, or Reset to restore their default dimensions. Closing the window can hide it to the tray after explanation and confirmation when the tray is available. Use explicit Quit to exit safely; closing the window is not a configurable background-mode preference or proof that transfers stopped. Illustrative sample. Controls may differ in your build; this image does not verify the complete task or its result.

Choose the affected connection before editing storage settings. Setting Desired default Supported range Cache quota 20 GiB 1–1024 GiB Auto clean Off Enable only for supported, eligible work Auto clean age 7 days 1–365 days The quota has no unlimited option. Saving a quota or cleanup choice does not establish that the running storage policy changed. Inspect the available application result and usage afterward. Unknown usage is not zero. Cleanup eligibility and protection rules still apply: a quota or age limit does not authorize removing unuploaded, edited, open, pinned or uncertain work. See storage. The cache location is managed. When a cache move is offered, use its destination review, approval and status controls. Editing a pathname in a settings file does not move cached files. Retain files and the operation details if a move fails.

Related-file and automatic pin-download defaults both start Off. They seed new pin reviews; changing them does not alter existing membership or consent. Downloads currently use a single full-file request; a multipart-upload request limit does not split a download into parallel parts. Ask your administrator for a supported policy. An optional approved enterprise CA requires its PEM file and matching lowercase, 64-character SHA-256 checksum. Use these steps when you receive a Sambafied tester ZIP. Read the included README first for that build's version, certificate thumbprint and known issues.

Extract the tester ZIP to a folder. Save your work, let active transfers finish and quit Sambafied, including its tray app, before updating. Keep your work folders and application data. If a test certificate is supplied, open the .cer file. In Details, find Thumbprint and compare it with the value in the supplied README. Stop if they do not match. For that matching certificate, choose Install Certificate, Local Machine, then Place all certificates in the following store. Select Trusted People and complete the administrator approval. Open the .msix file and choose Install or Update in Windows App Installer. Check that its version matches the build you received. Open Sambafied AEM from the Windows Start menu. The certificate step trusts the supplied self-signed tester certificate on this PC. Only use it for a tester package received from your Sambafied contact. A publicly trusted release does not require this test certificate step. Illustrative sample. After launching Sambafied, review its prerequisite checks.

Use the same steps with the next tester ZIP. Windows can update a compatible package with the same identity to a higher version. If it reports a different publisher or package conflict, ask your Sambafied contact for the migration steps before uninstalling anything. Installing the .msix from a tester ZIP does not subscribe you to the Sambafied update feed. See automatic updates for channel installs.

If .msix files do not open, install or update Microsoft App Installer, then retry. If Windows reports a missing VCLibs framework, send the exact error to your Sambafied contact and ask for the matching Microsoft framework package. The ordinary Visual C++ redistributable is not the same package. Do not delete work folders, recovery copies or application data to fix an installation error. Report the package version, Windows error and steps taken. Build-specific fixes and known issues remain in the README supplied with each ZIP.

documents.t: A local save and a confirmed AEM update are different events. Keep the work folder’s Author and account visible as you move from editing to publication.

Recall the original before editing. Save through the desktop application as usual, then inspect the candidate’s Changes surface. A saved local file is not a receipt that AEM received the change. The inspected development code tracks root- and principal-bound generations in a journal. The Changes surface presents immutable generations rather than inferring a destination from a filename.

For a candidate that enables the bounded local on-premises publication adapter: Confirm the connection, work folder, and destination asset. Review the captured local generation and any pending or uncertain operation. Use the candidate’s explicit publication action. Confirm the resulting remote state before considering the operation complete. Manual publication is the default in the inspected local contract. A preference can opt in to future new-file uploads. It is not blanket approval to overwrite existing assets.

The local contract uses an explicit Create version & upload mine path for existing edits or name collisions. It verifies a recoverable remote version before replacement. That recovery mechanism is not an atomic multiwriter lock. The reviewed local Author accepts stale conditional binary updates; a preflight comparison cannot guarantee that another user will not write between the check and replacement. For an uncertain response, stop and reconcile the remote result before repeating the action. See conflicts and recovery.

The Explorer-action implementation includes check-out and check-in for an eligible registered asset. Check-in releases the current user’s checkout only and refuses unresolved local work, pending or unknown jobs, and open writers under its inspected contract. Check-in does not upload. Do not use it as a shortcut to publish edits.

These local adapters do not establish complete production sync or Cloud Service binary-write acceptance. Local deletion is not propagated to AEM under the inspected publication contract. Other operations—such as moving, deleting, duplicating, or bulk uploading repository content—need their own explicit qualification. Use readiness when planning a workflow.
Choose the right connection before you browse or search. A result belongs to an Author, account, and configured DAM scope; the same filename in another connection is a different asset.

Browse assets in Windows Explorer after connecting to AEM. Open the work folder for the connection you want to use, then navigate to the asset's folder. Keep the active connection and account in view when you switch between work folders. Use your configured evaluation subtree. A failed or partial listing does not establish that an asset was deleted.

The inspected desktop Search command has a bounded on-premises QueryBuilder adapter. Local checks cover a known asset, no-match results, rejected queries, and rejection after logout. They do not qualify every query, multi-page ordering, permission changes, or Cloud Service search. A search should retain its connection context. Clearing a search should not switch the selected connection or change authentication. Collections, advanced metadata discovery, and complete parity across deployment targets need their own acceptance. They are not implied by a successful single-asset search.

Navigate to the registered work folder in Explorer and open a known test original. If it is still cloud-only, the agent must obtain the original before the file can be used. Opening a file depends on its desktop application association and the candidate's actual handling of that file. This site does not publish a creative-application compatibility matrix. A linked document may depend on other files and their paths. Do not infer that opening one original also qualifies automatic dependency retrieval or relinking.

The inspected Explorer-action implementation includes Open in AEM and Copy AEM link for a registered asset. The URL points to the authorized AEM environment; it does not grant someone else access or make the asset public. Native menu activation and visual behavior have separate qualification requirements. See readiness and troubleshooting.

The core idea is familiar: navigate your AEM assets in a desktop folder and open a file where you work. The current native preview uses Windows Cloud Files integration, with bounded local AEM evidence.

A named connection identifies the Author and configured DAM subtree. A new, empty NTFS work folder is registered and populated from a bounded namespace snapshot. Files begin as cloud-only placeholders. Opening a supported original requests its bytes through the agent. The preview stages and verifies the original before completing recall. The original folder-preview slice documents a maximum of 1,000 entries and 16 levels. Treat these as preview constraints, not a production scale promise. Remote changes are not equivalent to a continuously refreshed mirror; evaluate the exact candidate’s refresh behavior.

A placeholder is not a complete local copy. A file that has already been fully recalled can remain accessible after the provider stops or the user logs out. A cloud-only file cannot be newly recalled without the required running, authenticated provider. This bounded behavior does not establish a complete offline mode. Do not rely on every asset being available without a connection, or interpret a status icon as an offline guarantee.

Saving locally and publishing to AEM are distinct events. Later local development work adds a durable change journal and explicit publication flows for configured local on-premises profiles. Manual publication is the default; existing edits and collisions have an explicit version-and-upload path. These are bounded local adapters, not a production sync guarantee. Check readiness for the distinction between implemented work and accepted deployment targets. The inspected local publication contract does not propagate a local file deletion to AEM. Do not delete or relocate pending work to clear a warning. Preserve local bytes and unresolved operations for diagnosis.

Stop disconnects active provider work while retaining the registration and working files. It is not a request to delete the folder. Unregister removes native registration after identity and lifecycle checks. Windows can remove cloud-only or partially recalled placeholders during unregister. The default command refuses those entries; an explicit discard option exists and can remove them. Fully resident originals and ordinary local-edited files are retained under the documented lifecycle contract. Before unregistering, inspect the exact root, preserve local changes, and use the candidate’s matching instructions. A retained or partially initialized folder must not be silently adopted as a fresh mount.

Check the exact candidate, AEM target, authentication profile, file type, and desktop application together. Background API checks do not establish Explorer appearance, navigation entries, keyboard access, or creative-app behavior.
