Multiple AEM instances. Separate folders. One desktop experience. That is a central Sambafied DAM Client product goal: keep different asset repositories available simultaneously within the same familiar desktop workflow, while making each destination explicit.

Connection Author Work folder PROD Your production Author C:\users\sambafieduser\Sambafied\PROD STAGE Your staging Author C:\users\sambafieduser\Sambafied\STAGE DEV Your development Author C:\users\sambafieduser\Sambafied\DEV These are example connection names and paths. Replace sambafieduser with your Windows username and use the Author addresses supplied by your administrator. Keep production, staging and development work in separate folders; these examples do not move existing data or configure a connection automatically. The connection and mount commands take an explicit connection name and work-folder path. The agent model binds a root to its connection and principal. These are the primitives for separate mappings; their existence does not prove a fully qualified simultaneous multi-instance desktop experience.

Give each connection a recognizable name and record its intended Author and DAM subtree. Use a distinct, empty work-folder path for each new mapping. Confirm the signed-in identity and target before performing any operation. Evaluate each target and authentication profile independently. Do not treat moving files between two work folders as a qualified cross-instance migration workflow.

The complete experience needs evidence for simultaneous connections, independent sign-in and logout, restore after restart, destination clarity, publication routing, and failure isolation. Production on-premises and Cloud Service targets also need separate acceptance. Until that evidence is recorded, treat the multi-instance workflow as under development, not a released compatibility promise. Read getting started for the bounded single-target evaluation path and readiness for open gates.

AEM assets. Local, on your desktop. Sambafied DAM Client is a native Windows client being built to bring AEM Assets into the folders and desktop applications you already use. Our goal is simple: open Windows Explorer, find an asset in its AEM work folder, and work with it in your usual application. For teams using several AEM environments, each connection should have its own clearly named folder, available side by side. For a concrete open, edit, save and verify journey, read Desktop Experience.

AEM manages the assets. Your everyday work often happens elsewhere: placing an image in a layout, opening a video in an editor, or finding a file from an application's Open dialog. Moving between the repository, downloads and desktop tools can interrupt that work. Working across several brands or AEM environments adds another question: which repository does this file belong to? We are building Sambafied for people who want the Windows filesystem to be their everyday route into AEM. Its focus is familiar folders, clear destinations and less connection switching across desktop tasks.

The work folder is central to the experience. The desktop window provides connections, asset discovery and transfer status; the intended day-to-day workflow also reaches assets through Explorer and application file dialogs. The Windows preview has exercised a bounded AEM folder tree in Explorer with originals downloaded when opened. The aim is to make assets available without downloading the entire repository first. Check your build's folder access and limits before relying on a particular application workflow.

A team might use folders named Brand Studio, Production and Staging, each connected to a different AEM Author. The intended benefit is keeping the right assets within reach while making the destination of each file clear. Named connections and explicit work-folder paths are already part of the model. The complete simultaneous multi-instance experience remains under development. See multiple AEM instances for examples and evaluation checks.
documents.s: Give each AEM environment its own home

documents.t: Editing a local file and publishing a change to AEM are separate events. Sambafied's guides explain how to open an original, review local changes, upload deliberately and check transfer results. A local save alone is not confirmation that the server copy changed. This clarity is part of the workflow we are building, rather than a claim that existing clients lack upload controls. See opening and editing and transfers.
documents.s: Keep local work and uploads clear

documents.t: Option Where the workflow starts Sambafied's focus Adobe AEM desktop app A dedicated asset browser with browse, search, open, edit and upload actions. It already connects AEM to desktop applications. Put a native Windows work folder at the centre of everyday access, with per-instance folders as a central product goal. Adobe Asset Link Access to AEM assets from inside Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign. Adobe recommends Asset Link for those in-application workflows. Provide a folder workflow across Windows applications, with compatibility evaluated for each application and task. AEM in the browser Work directly in AEM's web interface and download files for desktop use when needed. Keep the connection between desktop work folders and their AEM destinations visible throughout local work. Adobe's desktop app already has on-demand downloads, and its v3 release notes describe automatic uploads of new files and collection synchronization. Those capabilities are not unique to Sambafied. Our distinction is the Explorer-first workflow and the goal of simultaneous, separate folders for different AEM instances. Read the detailed Adobe desktop app context for the server-switching comparison.
documents.s: How does it compare with existing options?

documents.t: Sambafied is a Windows development preview. Start with a small test asset and the instructions supplied for your beta build. Bounded local AEM and Explorer scenarios have been exercised; this is not a claim of production readiness or a supported Windows/AEM compatibility matrix. AEM on-premises and AEM as a Cloud Service are both in scope. Each environment and sign-in method needs its own testing. Simultaneous connections, offline work, conflict recovery, uploads and creative-application workflows still need build-specific confirmation. See readiness and limits. Want to help shape the client? Become a beta tester, or open the desktop user guide for installation, connections and asset tasks. Sambafied is independent of Adobe and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Adobe.
Settings should describe behavior available to the selected connection. A preference shown in a design contract is not evidence that it works for every deployment.

The desktop UI includes separate startup/window choices, an explicit remember-connection option, the connected work-folder path, and measured local usage. Open window at launch defaults to On. Startup is an optional saved request; its initial unchecked state is not proof of the Windows startup state. See Preferences for defaults, safe edits and application limits. Remembered sessions are checked against the Author again. An expired or rejected session needs sign-in; an unreachable Author is different from an invalid account. Changing a connection label does not move its files or retarget pending work. Use recognizable labels for separate AEM instances.

Closing the main window can leave the agent serving registered work folders. Pause stops provider work; resume attempts to reconnect it. Explicit Quit follows the candidate’s drain/recovery lifecycle. Do not assume that closing a window stops every transfer, or that pausing removes a folder’s registration. See the folder workflow.

Cloud-only placeholders differ from fully recalled originals and ordinary local edited files. Fully resident bytes can remain after stopping or logout, but that does not establish full offline support. Maintain enough storage for the original and any retained changes. The desired cache quota defaults to 20 GiB, with a supported range of 1–1024 GiB and no unlimited option. A saved quota is separate from the running policy and does not override protected work. A managed cache location is not a backup policy; use the offered cache-move review rather than editing paths or moving files manually.

Auto clean defaults to Off, with an age of 7 days when enabled unless changed; the supported age range is 1–365 days. It applies only to supported, eligible work and remains capability-gated. Enabling the saved preference does not establish that cleanup is active or that a particular root is eligible. Edited, open, pinned, unuploaded and uncertain work needs protection. Do not enable a setting merely because a CLI command exists. Check whether the exact root reports support and whether the candidate has the relevant qualification.

No production installer or upgrade procedure is published here yet. For development candidates, follow the matching package-identity instructions and retain registered provider identity while roots depend on it. Before removing a registration, preserve local changes and review stop and unregister. Cloud-only and partially recalled entries have different removal behavior from resident files.
Sambafied DAM Client is a development preview for Windows only. A public customer installer, supported Windows/AEM version matrix and production support offering are not available yet.

Obtain the application and instructions from your product contact. Confirm which AEM environments, sign-in methods and tasks your build supports. Begin with a small test asset and keep copies of local edits.

The complete simultaneous multi-instance desktop experience is still under development. Offline work, automatic sync, conflict recovery and production uploads need build-specific confirmation. Creative application compatibility, Explorer actions, accessibility and high-DPI behavior may vary by build. AEM on-premises and AEM as a Cloud Service connections require their own supported configuration. A successful connection to one environment does not establish compatibility with another. A completed security review or certification has not been announced. Do not treat preview availability as approval for production use.
Start with getting started, follow the desktop user guide, and check the availability notes in each topic. If something goes wrong, use troubleshooting and preserve local work before making changes.

Allow 30–45 minutes to test the installed Windows app against a local AEM Author. These are expected results to check, not a claim that a build already passes. Use Windows Explorer and AEM's browser interface to verify both sides; a green status alone is not sufficient.

For removal, device transfers and local file details, read Licensing. Install the supplied tester build and open Sambafied. Open About, then Manage licence. Enter the licence key supplied by Sambafied or your reseller and choose Activate. Confirm that the dialog reports a valid activation for this device. Close it and reopen licence management to check that activation was retained. Sambafied licensing is separate from AEM sign-in. Never put the key in a test report or screenshot. If activation fails, record the visible error without the key and mark the remaining cases Blocked. If the supplied evaluation build does not expose licensing, confirm that exception with your test coordinator and record it rather than assuming activation passed. Illustrative sample. Manage licence confirms activation and shows the offline expiry.

Download the sample ZIP pack (about 19 KB), or download files individually: Small image - PNG Sample document - PDF Editable file - TXT Extract the ZIP into an ordinary local folder before testing. For an individual file, use your browser's Save link as if it opens a preview. Upload sample-editable.txt through AEM's browser interface to your dedicated test DAM folder and confirm it shows Revision: 1. Open the connected copy in Windows Notepad, change it to Revision: 2, save and close, then verify a fresh original downloaded from AEM. The image and PDF are also marked Revision 1. If your AEM configuration rejects a sample file type, record that restriction as Blocked.

For a standard local AEM Author running on the tester's PC, use this Author URL: http://localhost:4502/ Use your actual Author address if the host or port differs. localhost refers to the PC running Sambafied. HTTP is permitted only for an explicitly configured loopback development Author; use HTTPS for normal network environments. Record the app build, Windows version, local Author URL and test account. Follow Connect to local AEM. Use a dedicated connection and work folder, with Automatic upload enabled. In AEM, create a dedicated DAM folder such as desktop-test-YYYYMMDD-initials. Use the sample image, PDF and editable text file above, or your own disposable equivalents. Seed the editable file in AEM with revision 1. Use disposable test assets only. Close editors before replacing assets from AEM. Agree a maximum wait for synchronization with the test coordinator before starting. Record elapsed time; do not wait indefinitely or treat a timeout as a pass.

ID Steps Expected result OP-01 Connect Sign in to local Author in Sambafied and select the connection's work folder. Login remains usable until completed or cancelled. Home shows the correct account and connected folder. OP-02 Browse and search Navigate to the test folder, search for an asset and open its preview/details. Correct assets, thumbnails and details appear. Loading finishes; failures show an understandable error. OP-03 Open from Explorer Choose Open Drive, find the revision 1 asset and open it in its normal application. The correct original downloads and opens. Check Explorer's Status column on the mapped drive. OP-04 Edit and save Change the revision to 2, save and close the editor. Download the original through AEM's browser interface into a separate folder. Automatic upload completes and the independently downloaded original contains revision 2. OP-05 Repeated saves Make two more edits, saving each, then close the editor. Check a fresh original downloaded from AEM. AEM contains the final revision. Pending/upload indicators clear and an unchanged file does not continually upload. OP-06 New local files Copy the image and PDF into a new subfolder inside the connected work folder. The folder and both assets appear in AEM. Downloaded originals open with the expected content. OP-07 Changes from AEM Upload a new asset in AEM's browser interface, then replace an existing test original there. Both changes reach the desktop/Explorer view. Opening the updated original shows the new content. Record propagation time. OP-08 Rename and move Rename a disposable asset in Explorer, then move it between two test subfolders. Check AEM after each operation. AEM shows the intended path with intact content and no duplicate or abandoned asset. Record any explicit unsupported-operation message. OP-09 Offline recovery Make only the tester-owned Author unavailable, or disconnect this test PC from it. Edit a previously downloaded asset and save. Restore access. Local edits survive. Disconnection/pending work is visible, then final content reaches AEM without manually copying it again. Do not interrupt a shared Author. OP-10 Restart recovery Save another edit, quit the desktop app and reopen it. Check Home, the work folder and a fresh AEM original. Settings and local edits survive. Synchronization resumes or has completed, and AEM contains the final content. OP-11 Download a copy Download the same asset twice into an ordinary local destination. Both copies open correctly, have distinct filenames and preserve existing destination files.

Conflict: While offline, edit a downloaded asset locally and have a second tester replace the same original in AEM. Reconnect. Check that conflicting content is preserved and the app explains how to resolve it. Connection isolation: With two test connections, switch between them and edit one disposable asset. Verify that it uploads only to its owning connection.

Record Pass / Fail / Blocked / Not run for each ID, including licensing. For a failure, include the build, asset path, steps, expected and actual result, elapsed sync time and a redacted screenshot. An unsupported operation is not a pass; record it for the coordinator to assess against the build's scope. Keep failed-case files and recovery copies until the defect is investigated. Remove only your disposable test assets after results are accepted. Never delete work folders, application data or another tester's files as cleanup. Run Testing with SaaS separately: local AEM results do not establish Cloud Service acceptance. See readiness and limits.

Allow 30–45 minutes, plus your environment's asset processing time, to test the installed Windows app with AEM as a Cloud Service Author. Use an approved test environment. These are expected results to check, not an assurance that every Cloud operation is supported by the supplied build.

For removal, device transfers and local file details, read Licensing. Install the supplied tester build and open Sambafied. Open About, then Manage licence. Enter the licence key supplied by Sambafied or your reseller and choose Activate. Confirm a valid activation for this device. Close and reopen licence management to check that activation was retained. The Sambafied licence does not grant Adobe account access. Never include the key in screenshots or reports. If activation fails, record the redacted error and mark dependent tests Blocked. If an evaluation build omits licensing, confirm and record that exception with the test coordinator rather than marking it passed. Illustrative sample. Manage licence confirms activation and shows the offline expiry.

Download the sample ZIP pack (about 19 KB), or download files individually: Small image - PNG Sample document - PDF Editable file - TXT Extract the ZIP into an ordinary local folder before testing. For an individual file, use your browser's Save link as if it opens a preview. Upload sample-editable.txt through AEM's browser interface to your dedicated test DAM folder and confirm it shows Revision: 1. Open the connected copy in Windows Notepad, change it to Revision: 2, save and close, then verify a fresh original downloaded from AEM. The image and PDF are also marked Revision 1. If your AEM configuration rejects a sample file type, record that restriction as Blocked.

Use your Cloud Service Author URL. For example: https://author-p999999-e9999999.adobeaemcloud.com/ This is an example address. Replace p999999 and e9999999 with the project and environment identifiers from your actual Author URL, or copy the complete URL supplied by your AEM administrator. Use the Author endpoint, not a delivery URL. Record the app build, Windows version, Cloud Author URL, organization and test account. Confirm that the account can browse, download, create and update assets in a dedicated test DAM subtree through AEM's browser interface. Follow Connect to AEM Cloud Service. Use the Author URL, a separate connection and a distinct work folder. Enable Automatic upload for that connection. Create a folder such as desktop-test-YYYYMMDD-initials. Use the sample image, PDF and editable text file above, or your own disposable equivalents. Seed the editable file in AEM with revision 1. Confirm the build's enabled Cloud operations and known issues with the coordinator. Record missing prerequisites as Blocked, not passed. Agree separate maximum waits for transfer and AEM processing. Record both timings; upload completion alone does not prove the asset is ready.

ID Steps Expected result SAAS-01 Sign in Add the Cloud Author connection. Complete Sign in with Adobe, organization SSO and MFA when requested. Login remains available while needed. The app validates the Author session and displays the correct account, environment and work folder. SAAS-02 Browse and search Navigate to the test folder, search for a seeded asset and inspect preview/details. Assets belong to the intended environment. Loading ends with real results or an understandable error. SAAS-03 Open original Use Open Drive and open the revision 1 asset from Explorer. The actual original downloads and opens in the expected application with correct content. Check the mapped drive's Status column. SAAS-04 Edit and save Change to revision 2, save and close the editor. Independently download the original through Cloud Author into a separate folder. Automatic upload completes and the downloaded original shows revision 2. Record transfer completion separately from AEM processing/readiness. SAAS-05 Repeated saves Save two further revisions, then close the editor and check a fresh Cloud Author download. The final revision reaches the correct asset. Pending indicators settle without repeatedly uploading unchanged content. SAAS-06 New uploads Copy the image and PDF into a new subfolder in the connected work folder. The folder and assets appear in Cloud Author. Independently downloaded originals match. Processing reaches a usable state; thumbnails/previews become available for supported formats. SAAS-07 Changes from Author Upload a new asset through Cloud Author and replace an existing test original after closing its local editor. The desktop/Explorer view receives both changes. Opening the updated original shows the new revision. Record propagation and processing time separately. SAAS-08 Rename and move Rename a disposable asset in Explorer, then move it between test subfolders. Check Cloud Author after each step. The intended remote path contains intact content without duplicate or abandoned assets. Record explicit unsupported-operation messages. SAAS-09 Offline recovery Disconnect only the test PC from the network. Edit a previously downloaded asset and save, then reconnect. Local edits survive, unavailable/pending state is clear and final bytes reach Cloud Author after reconnecting without manual re-copying. SAAS-10 Restart Save another edit, quit the desktop app and reopen it. Reauthenticate if requested. Connection settings and local content survive. Pending synchronization resumes or has finished; Cloud Author contains the final revision. SAAS-11 Download a copy Download the same asset twice to an ordinary local destination. Both copies open with correct content, have distinct names and preserve existing files. SAAS-12 Sign out and return Wait for transfers to finish and close editors. Sign out of the Cloud connection, then sign in again. The app shows a signed-out state without claiming new authenticated work succeeded. Existing local content survives; signing in restores the correct connection.

SSO cancellation/session expiry: Cancel sign-in once, then retry. If an approved test session expires naturally, check that reauthentication is clear and pending edits survive. Do not change organization identity settings to force expiry. Conflict: Edit a downloaded asset offline while a second tester replaces its Cloud Author original. Reconnect and check that both versions remain recoverable and conflict resolution is explained. Environment isolation: With separate local and Cloud connections, edit a disposable asset in one work folder. Verify that only its owning Author changes.

Record Pass / Fail / Blocked / Not run for each ID and licence activation. Include the build, Author environment, asset path, timings and redacted errors or screenshots. Exclude licence keys, passwords, session cookies and signed URLs. An unsupported operation is not a pass; ask the coordinator to assess its scope. Preserve failed-case assets and recovery copies until investigated. After results are accepted, remove only your disposable test assets. Keep existing work folders and application data. A local AEM pass or successful Cloud sign-in does not prove Cloud reads, uploads or processing: report each observed result separately. See Testing with OnPrem and readiness and limits.
First record the exact candidate revision, connection name, work-folder path, AEM target, action, and error. Keep session cookies, passwords, tokens, and sensitive asset names out of shared reports.

Confirm the Author URL and the intended account. A successful browser login alone does not prove that the client has a usable AEM session. Authentication profiles and endpoint access must be qualified for the target environment. Do not switch upload or authentication strategy merely because a request returns 401, 403, or 404. Check the selected profile and candidate’s documented support boundary.

Check that the path is new and empty, the filesystem and volume meet the candidate’s native preflight, and the agent has the required development package identity. A retained registration, foreign ownership, partial initialization, or an unqualified volume can block a mount. Preserve the folder and state. Do not recursively delete it or disable system protections to force a pass.
documents.s: A new work folder will not mount

documents.t: A cloud-only placeholder still needs its original bytes. Check that the agent is running, the connection is authenticated, and the original remains accessible in AEM. Use the candidate’s root-status command for the exact mount path. A changed remote observation, interrupted recall, or session expiry can reject an open. Capture the error rather than treating the placeholder as a downloaded copy.
documents.s: A file appears but will not open

documents.t: Native API success does not prove a navigation entry, menu, availability icon, or file dialog behaves as expected. Check the exact package identity and native registration, then compare with the candidate’s visual qualification notes. Do not infer production readiness from a background-only result.
documents.s: Explorer looks different from a background test

documents.t: A local save is not proof of remote publication. Inspect the candidate’s Changes surface and publication state. Pending or uncertain operations require reconciliation; repeated blind uploads can make diagnosis harder. Preserve the local edited file and the agent’s retained state. Complete sync and production publication acceptance remain open.
documents.s: My changes are not visible in AEM

documents.t: Read stop and unregister first. Stop, unregister, and delete are different operations. Cloud-only entries have distinct retention behavior from fully recalled files.
documents.s: I need to remove the work folder

documents.t: Skip the email thread and the Word document. Open the screen you want to talk about, put a pin on the part that needs work, and tell the team what you expected. Try it on the Transfers screen → Start where you noticed it In DAM Client, choose Give feedback on this screen. The deep link brings your recent steps into the portal. Open the published screenshot for the step you want to discuss and choose whether to include those steps with your feedback. Point to exactly what should change Suppose you’ve just uploaded a file and want to open its destination folder. Put a pin on the transfer row and write “Let me open the folder from here.” The pin shows where. Your words explain why. Give everyone the same view Submit your annotation, then use Link to this review to share the exact screenshot from that round. A teammate can open it, read your submitted comment, and add +1 if the same issue affects them.
documents.s: Give feedback on the UI you use

documents.t: Open the Feedback Portal and choose a project Give feedback from DAM Client Find a screen or follow a workflow Annotate a screen and submit feedback

In DAM Client, leave the screen or dialog you want to discuss visible. Choose the feedback icon beside Inbox, or open the main menu and choose Give feedback on this screen. Your default browser opens the DAM Client project. In App context, follow your recent steps to Feedback clicked here. Choose List layout for a chronological list, or Workflow layout to see the steps connected. Returning to the same screen can appear as a separate visit. Select the image for the step you want to review. The image is a published example of that screen and state. If a dialog was open when you clicked feedback, the app uses the dialog as the endpoint. If a step has no published screenshot, use Screens or Workflows to find a related capture and describe the difference in your comment. In Feedback, check Context from the app. Add an optional note under What were you trying to do?, or clear Include this app context with my feedback before submitting. Then submit and confirm your review.

The app includes its version and recent navigation in that window, using identifiers for workflows, screens, states and actions such as opening a dialog or going back. A long trail can omit earlier steps. The app keeps account details, AEM addresses, paths, filenames, search text and credentials out of the automatic context. The portal uses published screenshots rather than taking a picture of your desktop. Included context is visible with your submitted feedback under your GitHub identity. You control the text and images you add. A screenshot you attach yourself can show details that the automatic context excludes.

If the app reports a browser launch error, use its copy or retry option. Paste the copied link into your browser to keep the navigation context. If your installed version has no feedback action, open DAM Client feedback and find the screen manually. Older app links may open a matching screenshot or its workflow directly. If the portal reports invalid or unavailable context, you can still review a screen from the gallery.
documents.s: If the browser or screen does not open

documents.t: Open Screens. Use Find a screen, then narrow the results by State, Window size or Surface. For example, choose the loading state to comment on what you see while waiting. Duplicates lets you group identical images or see each scenario separately. If a screen disappears after you review it, change Review status from Remaining screens to All screens. Use With feedback or the ratings filter to revisit earlier work. Archived screens contains read-only captures removed from the current cycle.

Choose Workflows and select a journey. In the Journey map, click an arrow to inspect the action or condition that leads to the next screen. Locate destination on map moves to the destination card. Open destination opens its screenshot. Use List view if you prefer to read the sequence. All states shows capture variations and Stage overview groups them by stage. A missing capture or unmapped state means the round has no published image or verified route for that step. The workflow map describes the published examples. To show the steps you actually took, start feedback from the app.

Open a screenshot and expand Compare in the Review panel. Select an available before image to view it alongside the current one. Open Scenarios for the scenario and capture details. Use Link to this review to share the exact round and image. The link identifies the screenshot, so submit your comments separately if you want others to read them. If an older link says its round or image is unavailable, use Open latest feedback to browse the current round and select the screen again.
documents.s: Compare or link to a capture

documents.t: Open a screenshot. In Feedback, choose a score from 1 to 10 and describe the change you want in What should change?. For example, “When the upload finishes, show the destination folder so I can check the file.” Choose Add image or paste a screenshot if it helps. Remove customer details, filenames and account information from any attachment you share. Use the Annotations panel to place a Pin at a point, draw a Rectangle around an area or use an Arrow to indicate direction. Select a mark to add or edit its comment. Use Delete to remove the selected mark or Undo to reverse an edit. Hide annotations temporarily hides your marks. On narrow screens, open the Annotations or Review drawer to reach these tools. To comment on a named button or field, choose Select, enable Show controls and click its outline. Type in Annotation comment and press Enter to attach the comment to that component. Shift+Enter adds a line. If the screenshot has no outline for your target, use a pin or rectangle.

Check the save status in Feedback before leaving. Previous and Next save the current review as you move. You can use Ctrl+Left or Ctrl+Right outside text fields. Alt+1 through Alt+9 set a score. Alt+0 scores 10 and advances. Return to the gallery and sign in with GitHub to submit your saved feedback to the round issue. Drafts belong to the browser and round where you made them. Use the same browser profile when you return. Wait for confirmation and keep the GitHub submission receipt. If the outcome is uncertain, choose Check this same submission to look up the original attempt. To track the beta tester reward, open Rewards in the licence portal. Submit your rating and testimonial under Profile. Clear local feedback clears this round’s browser scores, comments, annotations and reviewed status. Submitted feedback and receipts are retained.

Sign in, open a screen and expand Everyone’s submitted feedback. You can read the latest confirmed feedback per reviewer in each round. Select +1 on a submitted annotation if the same issue affects you. Select it again to remove your vote. Select the count to see who is affected. Older comments retain their original round. If the image changed, read the earlier annotation notes against the original image. You can delete your own submitted screen feedback from the shared view. The original submission and GitHub issue comment remain in the audit history.

Use the Sambafied License Portal to find your licences and manage device activations. Sign in with the email associated with your licence or company invitation. Overview shows your licence status, available downloads, rewards progress, and client count for partner owners. Workspace covers each menu section, switching accounts, profile, downloads, rewards, and feedback. Personal covers account setup, the Personal beta trial and activation, plus device management and payments. Company covers partner setup and client registration, administrator invitations and handover, and Corporate trials and billing. A Personal licence belongs to one named person. A Corporate licence belongs to the company and covers its staff. Company administrators use the portal to manage access and the Corporate licence. Staff can activate the desktop app with the company's licence key. The desktop licensing guide covers activation, offline use and uninstalling on Windows.

Open the Sambafied invitation sent to your company email. It expires after 12 hours. If it expires, ask the sender to issue a fresh invitation. If you already have an account at the invited address, choose Sign in to claim. Otherwise, create your administrator account from the invitation. Sign in to the License Portal and open Profile → User profile → Company administration. If you manage several companies, select the company you want from the list.

In Company administration, enter a colleague's work email and select Send invitation. They claim access using their own sign-in. You can cancel a pending invitation or remove an additional administrator from the company. Each administrator can manage the selected company's licences, device activations, invoices and billing when available, and administrator invitations. Set up at least one additional administrator so support can continue if the primary administrator is unavailable. Staff who only need to activate the desktop app use the company licence key and do not need admin accounts.

Open the company and find Primary administrator transfer. Select an existing full administrator, including yourself if eligible, and choose Request transfer. Give the request reference to Sambafied support. Sambafied verifies the requested change with the company before approving it. Additional administrators can keep working during the review. After approval, the former primary becomes an additional administrator and can be removed. The transfer keeps the company's existing licence and billing references. If a departing administrator already knew the shared desktop key, contact Sambafied to coordinate key rotation.

Partner team access is scoped to the selected partner workspace. An Owner opens Profile → Partner team, enters a colleague's email and selects Send invitation. The colleague signs in or creates an account with that email, then accepts the invitation. The Partner roster shows their address, role and status. Use Resend email or Cancel invitation while it is pending. Approve existing account is available for a verified invited account. Owners can use Change Role to select Owner, Admin or Member. Assign a second Owner before lowering the last Owner's role. Admins can edit the partner profile and invite client companies. Members can view the partner profile and client list.

Create a License Portal account using your work email and verify it. Ask your Sambafied contact to approve your partner access. Sign in and open Profile → Partner profile. If you belong to several partner workspaces, select the one you want to edit. Enter your business name, website and contact email. Upload an optional PNG, JPEG or WebP logo. Add an optional formatted description, choose whether the business appears in the directory, and select Save partner profile. Your business name appears in future company invitations. Invitation emails come from Sambafied.

In My Clients → Register a company, enter the legal company name, the first administrator's work email and the company billing email. Select Send company invitation. The administrator opens the email and claims the company using the invited address. Check Registered companies. Ready for billing means the administrator claimed the company. To send a fresh link after expiry, submit the same company details again. If you are registering your own company, enter your own portal email as the administrator email. Open the invitation and choose Sign in to claim with your existing account. You keep your partner access and become the company's primary administrator. For a client company, invite the person authorised to administer it. Your partner role lets you register and onboard clients. Access to a client's licence keys, devices and invoices requires company administrator membership. Where Add a company without inviting anyone is available, a partner owner can start a 14-day managed Corporate trial from My Clients. Use Get licence key to share the key through the client's approved channel. Billing actions appear according to the selected workspace and company's access. See company administrators for claiming access and inviting colleagues, and Corporate trials and billing for what happens after the claim.

An eligible partner can start a managed 14-day trial in My Clients. If your company claimed a registration by invitation, ask your partner or Sambafied contact to arrange a trial. A trial has a fixed expiry and requires no payment. A paid subscription starts only when Checkout completes.

Sign in to the License Portal as a company administrator. Open Profile → User profile → Company administration and select the company. Under Company licences, open the Corporate licence to check its status and expiry or reveal its key. Share the key only through your company's approved internal channel. Staff follow the desktop activation guide. Administrators can use Manage devices on the licence to release a PC activation. Deactivation keeps files and settings on the PC and an offline authorisation may remain valid until its expiry.
documents.s: Find the licence and activate staff devices

documents.t: Ready for billing shows that the company has been claimed. Checkout is available only for eligible companies. When billing is available for your company, the partner prepares Checkout and a company administrator completes it with the company's billing details. Open Company administration > Company billing to find paid invoices and the Manage billing option when they are available. If you manage multiple companies, select the correct one first. Each company has its own invoices and licence. See pricing and Corporate enquiries if you need to discuss a paid licence.
A Personal licence is issued to you as a named individual.

Open the License Portal and select Create an account. Enter your email and open the verification link from Sambafied. The link expires in 15 minutes. Request a fresh email if it has expired. Enter your name and choose a password, then return to Sign in. Open My licences to see the licences assigned to this account. If you already have an account, sign in with the email you used to register. If you need to recover access, contact your Sambafied representative.

A new verified beta account receives a 14-day Personal trial. If setup shows as pending, sign in again or select Retry trial setup on Overview when it appears. Retrying keeps the original expiry. For the beta tester reward, use the same account to download the beta from the portal, activate your Personal licence, and submit a testimonial. Track your progress in Rewards. After a Sambafied operator approves the reward, open Rewards to receive a free 12-month Personal licence. See the Sambafied beta programme for details.

Open My licences and use the copy icon on the Personal licence card. To read the key, choose View licence and Reveal key. With an internet connection, open About → Manage licence in Sambafied Desktop. Sign in with the same Sambafied account, then paste the key and select Activate. Check the activation status and expiry shown in the app. Keep the key private and out of screenshots or support messages. For offline refresh, moving PCs and uninstalling, see the desktop licensing guide.

Sign in to the License Portal. Open My licences and choose Manage devices on your Personal licence, or open Devices and select the licence. Find the PC by name and activation details. Select Deactivate PC and confirm that you have chosen the right device. To move to a new PC, follow the desktop activation guide on that PC. Deactivation releases the remote activation and keeps files and settings on the PC. An offline PC may keep its current authorisation until the offline expiry. If you still have the old PC, use the desktop app's Deactivate this device action to remove the saved licence from that PC.

Payments is its own section in the sidebar. If payment history is available, it shows paid invoices. Check the payment date, invoice reference and amount. Use the billing options shown for your account when available. Checkout and billing controls appear when available for your account. If you need a copy of an invoice or help with a licence, contact Sambafied.

Section What you can do Overview Check licence status and expiry, open Downloads and Rewards, and see My Clients when available. My licences Browse assigned licence cards. Open a licence or copy its key using the icon beside the masked key. Devices Select a licence and manage its PC activations. Downloads Read Windows release notes and download an available installer. Rewards Track your beta activity and reward licence. Partners Browse listed partners and contact a partner. Profile Edit your user profile and testimonial. Partner accounts also have workspace profile and team options. My Clients Manage companies for the selected partner workspace when your role allows it. Payments Find payment history and billing actions available for the signed-in account. Help & guides Open the licensing and desktop guides.

Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar and select Add another account. Enter that account's credentials and select Sign in and switch. Use the same menu to move between signed-in accounts. Check the email shown there before copying a key, changing a profile or managing devices.

Open Downloads. The Beta filter shows the latest available beta. Use Stable for production releases or All releases to browse both. Read the release notes and choose the Windows download. Follow the tester installation guide.

Use the same account to download the beta from Downloads, activate a Personal licence and try the app, then submit a testimonial. Rewards shows which steps are complete. After Sambafied approves the reward, open Rewards to receive the free 12-month Personal licence. It then appears in My licences. Use desktop feedback to report a problem.

In Profile → User profile, use Edit name to update your name. Add an optional website, profile picture and description, then select Save user profile. Use the description controls and preview to check formatting. In Profile → Testimonial, choose a star rating and enter your feedback. Selecting Submit testimonial gives Sambafied permission to share it. Positive feedback is not required.

In Partners, select a listed partner's name to view its description when provided. Choose Contact to send an enquiry. If you manage a partner workspace, see partner setup and client registration. Use Feedback in the workspace header to review the portal screenshots. Open a screen in the License Portal feedback gallery to leave feedback about it. See how to share feedback for draft and submission options.
